---
title: "ggnomics"
subtitle: "Composable, ggplot2-style genomics visualization for Python"
---

`ggnomics` provides ggplot2-style visualizations for bulk, single-cell, and
multimodal genomics in Python. Its plotting functions work with tidy
`pandas` data and common genomics containers, including AnnData and BiocPy's
`SingleCellExperiment` and `SummarizedExperiment`.

The result is a [plotnine](https://plotnine.org) plot that remains yours to
adapt:

```python
import ggnomics as gg
import plotnine as p9

p = gg.plot_umap(adata, color="cluster")
p + p9.theme_bw() + p9.labs(title="Cell populations")
```

Start with [Getting started](getting-started.qmd), follow one of the
end-to-end workflows, or browse the [plot gallery](plot-gallery.qmd) for a
particular figure.

## Workflows

* **[Getting started](getting-started.qmd)** introduces DataFrame, SCE, and
  AnnData input and shows how to customize the returned plots.
* **[Single-cell analysis with scranpy](single-cell-scranpy.qmd)** follows a
  mouse brain dataset from quality control to clustering and UMAP.
* **[Bulk RNA-seq](bulk-rnaseq.qmd)** uses PyDESeq2 to analyse a rice
  salt-stress experiment.
* **[Multimodal](multimodal.qmd)** combines RNA and ADT measurements from
  CITE-seq data.
* **[Specialized plots](specialized-plots.qmd)** covers abundance,
  pseudobulk QC, statistics, significance brackets, palettes, heatmaps, and
  immune repertoires.
* **[Plot gallery](plot-gallery.qmd)** provides a compact reference organized
  by plot family.

## What's supported

| Container | Package | Typical use |
|---|---|---|
| `pd.DataFrame` | pandas | Tidy plotting tables and model results |
| `AnnData` | anndata / scverse | Single-cell data in scverse workflows |
| `SingleCellExperiment` | BiocPy `singlecellexperiment` | Single-cell assays, metadata, and reduced dimensions |
| `SummarizedExperiment` | BiocPy `summarizedexperiment` | Bulk assays and sample metadata |
| `MuData` | mudata / scverse | Measurements across several modalities |

Because `SummarizedExperiment` does not store reduced dimensions,
embedding plots require either explicit coordinates or a richer container.
For bulk assays, `ggnomics.bulk_pca` computes and plots PCA scores directly.
The [Getting started](getting-started.qmd) guide shows the supported paths in
more detail.

## One plotting interface

The public `plot_*` functions use Python's `singledispatch`: the function
name and main arguments stay the same while the input container determines
how data are extracted. The DataFrame implementation supplies the public
docstring shown by `help()` and in Jupyter. Adapters for AnnData, BiocPy, and
MuData register automatically when their corresponding packages are
installed.

[Getting started §7](getting-started.qmd#7-how-dispatch-works)
explains the design and shows how to inspect the registered implementations.

## Build on the returned plot

Most functions return an ordinary `ggplot`, so plotnine layers, scales,
themes, coordinates, and labels can be added directly. This keeps the
convenient genomics defaults without limiting the final figure.

```python
p = gg.plot_umap(adata, color="cluster")
p + p9.theme_bw() + p9.labs(title="My figure")
```

Multi-panel functions such as `plot_pseudobulk_qc`,
`plot_scatter_marginal`, and `plot_embedding_panel` return a
`plotnine.composition.Compose`. They can be arranged with plotnine's `|` and
`/` operators or with ggnomics helpers such as `hstack`, `vstack`, and
`grid`.

## Optional backends

The core installation provides the DataFrame interface. Container-specific
support can be added through optional extras:

```bash
pip install "ggnomics[anndata]"    # AnnData / scverse
pip install "ggnomics[sce]"        # SingleCellExperiment (BiocPy)
pip install "ggnomics[se]"         # SummarizedExperiment (BiocPy)
pip install "ggnomics[multimodal]" # MuData
pip install "ggnomics[stats]"      # significance brackets (scipy, statsmodels)
pip install "ggnomics[pca]"        # PCA utilities
pip install "ggnomics[umap]"       # ggnomics.sc_umap
pip install "ggnomics[all]"        # everything above
```

The workflow guides also use `scranpy`, PyDESeq2, Marsilea, `scrnaseq`,
`pyexpressionatlas`, and `experimenthub`. These are analysis or data-access
packages used alongside ggnomics rather than runtime dependencies of the
plotting library.
